source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: On Day 2, each participant received a 40-second low-intensity tFUS stimulation targeting either the right amygdala (tFUS group) or white matter (control group).

flags.reason: 80 participants were recruited and stated to have 'participated in the two-day tFUS experiment', but only 52 were included in the behavioural analysis (51 for fMRI) after post-hoc exclusions for data quality; enrolled number (80) is reported here.
tFUS increased CMA BOLD activity but decreased CMA-insula/IFG-OFC connectivity and impaired behaviour; the net excitatory/inhibitory direction is not straightforward, hence mixed_or_unclear.
The paper does not state whether assignment to tFUS vs. control (white matter) group was randomised.

readout_other: facial expression recognition task accuracy (fearful/neutral/happy); generalized PPI functional connectivity analysis
direction_notes: tFUS increased right CMA BOLD activity during emotional face processing (excitatory-like) while simultaneously decreasing CMA-right insula and CMA-left IFG/OFC functional connectivity and impairing fearful/emotional face recognition accuracy (inhibitory-like effect on connectivity and behaviour).
safety_notes: There were no adverse effects of tFUS in both groups, participants did not report any discomfort or annoying feelings during and after the sonication.

timing.protocol_description: The burst length was 30 ms, and the period (the length of time between the start of each burst) was 100 ms; in other words, 30 ms bursts of ultrasound was produced every 100 ms (duty cycle = 30%, pulse repetition frequency = 10 Hz). The total stimulation lasted 40s. On Day 2, each participant received a 40-second low-intensity tFUS stimulation targeting either the right amygdala (tFUS group) or white matter (control group).
